subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
source: Continues the school Drive Quran folder progression (TPS Quran Tracker tajweed rules) into Year 11; classical tajweed (Hafs 'an 'Asim) and tadabbur method; Qur'an text per the Madinah mushaf

lessons.title: The tajweed map: Al-Fatihah line by line
objectives: Pull together all rule families from Years 7-10
Find every rule in Al-Fatihah
Choose personal priorities for the final year

keywords.def: the places from which letters are pronounced
the qualities of letters
the rules of tajweed

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.
Name the rule families: makharij, sifat, noon and meem, madd, raa and laam, waqf.
Recite Al-Fatihah from memory.

teach.heading: Six families of rules
bullets: Noon sakinah, tanween and meem sakinah
Madd, raa and laam, waqf and ibtida'
teach.note: Draw the map as six boxes on the board and ask pupils to add one rule to each from memory. Explain that Year 11 is about mastery and about passing the Qur'an on. Ask: which family do you find hardest?

teach.heading: Fatihah: first half
bullets: lillahi rabbil-'alamin: light lam, light raa
yawm: waw sakinah after fatha, soft, no madd
teach.note: Recite the basmalah and verses 1-4. In لِلَّهِ the lam follows kasra so it is light. In رَبِّ the raa has kasra, so it is light. In الرَّحْمَٰنِ the lam merges into raa. In مَالِكِ the alif is madd tabi'i, 2 counts.

teach.heading: Fatihah: second half
bullets: Iyyaka: shaddah on yaa, hold it
Ihdinas-sirat: start with kasra, sad is heavy
teach.note: إِيَّاكَ: shaddah on yaa; do not shorten. نَسْتَعِينُ: on stopping, madd 'arid 2, 4 or 6. اهْدِنَا: starting on hamzat al-wasl, third letter has kasra so start with kasra. Ask pupils for the reason, not just the answer.

teach.heading: Fatihah: last ayah
teach.note: أَنْعَمْتَ: noon sakin before 'ayn, clear. عَلَيْهِمْ غَيْرِ: meem sakin before ghayn, izhar shafawi, no merging. وَلَا الضَّالِّينَ: alif then a shaddah on lam, madd lazim kalimi muthaqqal, 6 counts. Misconception: shortening this madd.

teach.heading: Priorities
bullets: List the three rules you find hardest
Link each to a surah you know
Practise for ten minutes a day
teach.note: Pupils copy the grid and rate every family: secure, nearly, not yet. They choose three priorities and put dates on the review. Close with a dua for steadfastness in the final year.

practice: Why is the lam light in لِلَّهِ?
What is the rule on the meem in عَلَيْهِمْ غَيْرِ?
How many counts in وَلَا الضَّالِّينَ and why?
independent: Mark all rules in Al-Fatihah on a printed copy
Sort rules by family on a map
Write three priorities with practice dates
exit: Name one rule from each of two families.
Which of your priorities will you start tonight?
lessons.homework: Practise your three priority rules daily with examples from three different surahs.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: map with sentence frames and colour codes. Stretch: build a one-page rule summary for a younger pupil.

lessons.title: Mistakes in recitation: spotting and correcting kindly
objectives: Distinguish clear mistakes (lahn jali) from subtle ones (lahn khafi)
Spot common errors in Al-Fatihah
Give kind, accurate correction

keywords.def: a clear mistake that changes a letter or vowel
a subtle mistake against the rules of tajweed
sincere advice given for someone's benefit

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.
What was the difference between major and minor mistakes in Year 5?
Recite Ayat al-Kursi, first phrase.

teach.heading: Two kinds of mistake
teach.note: Link to Year 5. Lahn jali changes a letter or a vowel and can change the meaning. Lahn khafi is subtler: weak ghunnah, short madd, wrong heaviness. Ask: which should we fix first? Clear mistakes, then the subtle ones.

teach.heading: Clear mistakes: examples
teach.note: أَنْعَمْتَ means 'You have favoured', أَنْعَمْتُ would mean 'I have favoured', which changes the meaning. Say each aloud. Ask pupils why the shaddah in إِيَّاكَ matters. Collect other examples they know.

teach.heading: Subtle mistakes: examples
bullets: Heavy raa read light, light lam read heavy
teach.note: Each subtle error is a loss of beauty and accuracy. Demonstrate: say إِنَّ with and without ghunnah. Say الرَّحْمَٰنِ with a heavy and a light raa. Ask pupils to identify which is correct and why. Be sensitive: use the teacher's voice as the model.

teach.heading: Correcting with adab
bullets: Give one correction at a time
teach.note: Teach nasihah: private, kind, specific. A model sentence: 'I loved your steady pace. One thing to check is the madd in الضَّالِّينَ.' Role-play in pairs. Remind pupils to accept correction humbly too.

teach.heading: Error hunt
teach.note: Play three short recordings you have made containing planted errors (for example a missing shaddah, a short madd, a light lam in a heavy position). Pupils note the error, the type and the correction. Discuss answers.

practice: Is reading أَنْعَمْتُ for أَنْعَمْتَ lahn jali or khafi? Why?
Give one example of lahn khafi.
Write one kind sentence of correction.
independent: Complete an error log with six errors, type and correction
Role-play a kind correction for a partner
Write a short guide: how to accept correction well
exit: What is the difference between lahn jali and lahn khafi?
What makes correction an act of nasihah?
lessons.homework: Record yourself reciting Al-Fatihah, find two errors and write how to fix them.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: error log with examples. Stretch: write five planted-error examples for the class.

lessons.title: Surat Al-Kahf 18:1-10: reading and rules
objectives: Recite 18:1-10 accurately
Apply noon, tanween and silah rules in context
Use the sakta in ayah 1 correctly

keywords.def: a short pause without breath
hiding the noon sound with ghunnah
a cave

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.
Recite 67:1-4.
What is the rule for tanween before lam?

teach.heading: Listen and recite
bullets: We read the first ten ayat
teach.note: Recite ayah 1: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَنزَلَ عَلَىٰ عَبْدِهِ الْكِتَابَ وَلَمْ يَجْعَل لَّهُ عِوَجَا. Pupils echo. Explain that these ten ayat begin the surah and we will learn them by heart in the coming weeks.

teach.heading: Ayat 1-3: rules
bullets: Sakta after 'iwaja, no breath, then qayyiman
teach.note: In ayah 1 the mushaf marks a sakta after عِوَجَا: a short pause without breath before قَيِّمًا. قَيِّمًا لِّيُنذِرَ: tanween before lam, idghaam without ghunnah. يُنذِرَ: noon sakin before dhal, ikhfa. ayah 3: stop on أَبَدًا with madd 'iwad.

teach.heading: Ayat 4-6: rules
bullets: bihi min 'ilmin: silah sughra, then izhar
teach.note: وَيُنذِرَ: ikhfa. بِهِ مِنْ عِلْمٍ: haa between two vowels, silah sughra; مِنْ عِلْمٍ: noon before 'ayn, izhar halqi. بَاخِعٌ نَّفْسَكَ: tanween then noon, idghaam bi-ghunnah. إِن لَّمْ يُؤْمِنُوا: noon before lam, idghaam without ghunnah.

teach.heading: Ayat 7-10: rules
teach.note: زِينَةً لَّهَا: tanween then lam. صَعِيدًا جُرُزًا: tanween fatha then jim, ikhfa. أَمْ حَسِبْتَ: meem sakin before haa, izhar shafawi. مِن لَّدُنكَ: noon before lam, idghaam bila ghunnah, then the noon of لَدُنكَ before kaf, ikhfa. Ask pupils to explain why.

teach.heading: Stops and practice
bullets: Recite in pairs and check rules
teach.note: Ayat ending with tanween fatha: أَبَدًا، وَلَدًا، أَسَفًا، عَمَلًا، رَشَدًا. At stops these end with a long alif, madd 'iwad. Pupils recite 1-5 in pairs and then 6-10. Partner ticks rules and stops.

practice: What is a sakta and where is it in ayah 1?
Which rule applies to صَعِيدًا جُرُزًا?
Why is there no silah in عَبْدِهِ الْكِتَابَ?
independent: Recite 18:1-5 and mark every rule
Recite 18:6-10 and mark every rule
Peer assess using the checklist
exit: Name two ikhfa examples in the passage.
Why do we use madd 'iwad on أَبَدًا when we stop?
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: chunked audio, colour-coded rules. Stretch: explain the sakta and why it is used, then teach it to a partner.

lessons.title: Surat Al-Kahf 18:1-10: meaning and reflection
objectives: Explain the meaning of ayat 1-10
Link 18:7 with 67:2
Reflect on the dua of the youths in ayah 10

keywords.def: crookedness, any fault
adornment
young men

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.
Recite 18:1-5.
What did 67:2 say about our test?

teach.heading: Ayat 1-3: Praise and guidance
bullets: All praise is for Allah, who sent down the Book
He placed no crookedness in it
It warns of severe punishment and gives glad tidings
teach.note: Read the meanings of 18:1-3. The Book is straight, with no fault. It warns and gives good news: believers who do good deeds have a good reward, remaining in it forever. Ask: why do both warning and good news appear together?

teach.heading: Ayat 4-6: A grave claim
bullets: It warns those who say Allah has a child
They have no knowledge of this
The Prophet ﷺ was grieving over them
teach.note: 18:4-5 condemn the claim that Allah has taken a child. Ayah 6 is gentle toward the Prophet ﷺ: you might destroy yourself with grief over them if they do not believe. Ask: what does this show about his care for people?

teach.heading: Ayat 7-8: The test of the earth
bullets: It is a test: who is best in deeds?
Everything on it will become barren ground
teach.note: Link 18:7 to 67:2: both speak of ahsanu 'amalan. Ask: how does beauty become a test? The earth will become barren (sa'idan juruza). Discuss how this should affect the way we treat worldly things: use them, do not worship them.

teach.heading: Ayat 9-10: The cave
bullets: The People of the Cave are one sign among many
The youths took refuge in the cave
They made dua for mercy and right guidance
teach.note: These two ayat introduce the story; the rest comes later in the surah. Read the dua of ayah 10: Our Lord, grant us mercy from Yourself and prepare for us right guidance in our affair. Pupils copy it. Ask: when could you use this dua?

teach.heading: The protection
bullets: Reported in Sahih Muslim by Abu al-Darda'
Memorising the first ten ayat protects from the Dajjal
Many Muslims also read Al-Kahf on Fridays
teach.note: State the hadith carefully: in Sahih Muslim it is reported that whoever memorises the first ten ayat of Surat Al-Kahf is protected from the Dajjal. For the practice of reading the surah on Fridays, ask your teacher about the evidence and scholars' views. Close with the dua of ayah 10.

practice: How does 18:7 link with 67:2?
What is the dua in 18:10?
What did Allah say to the Prophet ﷺ about his grief in 18:6?
independent: Write the meaning of each ayah in your own words
Create a mind map of the themes of ayat 1-10
Write a tadabbur paragraph on the dua in ayah 10
exit: When will you use the dua of the youths?
lessons.homework: Write 150 words: what 18:7 teaches me about how to treat the beauty of this world.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: translation chart and picture prompts. Stretch: research one theme from the rest of Al-Kahf in a recognised tafsir.

lessons.title: Al-Fatihah: a conversation with Allah
objectives: Explain the meaning of each ayah of Al-Fatihah
Describe the hadith of the prayer divided in two
Reflect on how to pray with presence

keywords.def: praise coupled with love and glorification
the straight path
humility and presence of heart in prayer

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.
Recite Al-Fatihah with its rules.
Say the meaning of ar-Rahman ar-Rahim.

teach.heading: Ayat 1-4: Who Allah is
bullets: Praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds
The Most Gracious, the Most Merciful
Master of the Day of Recompense
teach.note: Take each phrase slowly in English. In the Hafs recitation we read مَالِكِ, Master. Ask: what do the names Rabb, Rahman, Rahim and Malik teach us? Care, mercy and accountability together.

teach.heading: Ayat 5-7: What we ask
bullets: You alone we worship and seek help from
Guide us to the straight path
The path of those You blessed, not those who went astray
teach.note: Ayah 5 is the turning point from speaking about Allah to speaking to Him. Ayah 6 is the greatest need: guidance. Ayah 7 describes the path through the blessed ones. Scholars explain the two groups to avoid as those who know the truth and turn away, and those who lose the way.

teach.heading: The prayer divided
bullets: Sahih Muslim: Allah says He divided the prayer
The servant says Alhamdu lillah; Allah says: My servant praised Me
Half is for Allah, half for the servant
teach.note: The hadith is reported by Abu Hurayrah in Sahih Muslim. When the servant says each part, Allah responds. When the servant says 'You alone we worship and seek help from', Allah says that is between Him and His servant, and the servant will have what he asks. Ask: how does this change how you say the Fatihah in salah?

teach.heading: Praying with presence
bullets: Say each ayah as a reply
Think of the meaning, not only the sound
teach.note: Teach practical techniques: slow down slightly, think of the response from Allah, and focus on one phrase each prayer. Pupils practise silently. Note that khushu' is a goal built over time; do not discourage those who struggle.

teach.heading: My tadabbur
bullets: Write what it asks of you
teach.note: Pupils write a short piece connecting one ayah to a personal change, such as being more grateful (ayah 2) or more mindful of accountability (ayah 4). Share one anonymously.

practice: What happens, according to the hadith, when the servant says 'Alhamdu lillahi rabbil-'alamin'?
Which ayah is the turning point from speaking about Allah to speaking to Him?
What are we asking for in ayah 6?
independent: Write a one-line meaning for each ayah
Draw the dialogue between servant and Lord
Write a short tadabbur on one ayah
exit: Which ayah of Al-Fatihah speaks most to you now?
What is one way to bring more presence to your recitation in salah?
lessons.homework: Pray two rak'ahs this week thinking of the meaning of Al-Fatihah ayah by ayah, then write what you noticed.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: ayah-by-ayah translation chart. Stretch: compare the tafsir of Al-Fatihah in two recognised tafsirs.

lessons.title: Reading translations and tafsir wisely
objectives: Explain what a translation of the Qur'an can and cannot do
Use context to avoid misreading an ayah
Know when to ask a qualified scholar

keywords.def: an attempt to express the meaning in another language
the surrounding words, ayat and circumstances
the reasons or occasions of revelation

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.
What are the sources of tafsir?
What is the difference between tafsir and tadabbur?

teach.heading: What translation can do
bullets: It renders meanings, not the Qur'an itself
The Arabic text is the Qur'an
teach.note: Explain that a translation is a human attempt at the meaning and cannot replace the Arabic. Compare two English renderings of 1:5 if available. Ask: why might two translators choose different words?

teach.heading: Always read the whole sentence
bullets: Quote 4:43: do not approach prayer while intoxicated
The ayah continues: until you know what you say
teach.note: 4:43 is a useful example: the ayah continues with 'until you know what you are saying'. Show how stopping early would give a false impression. Similarly 107:4-5: 'woe to those who pray, who are heedless of their prayer'. Ask: what changes when we read the whole phrase?

teach.heading: Context and sources
bullets: Know the Arabic language and the Sunnah
teach.note: 2:256 says there is no compulsion in religion, and the following words say that the right path has become distinct from error. Show how a tafsir explains the context. Name tafsirs such as Tafsir al-Tabari, Tafsir Ibn Kathir and Tafsir al-Sa'di. Pupils choose one to look up.

teach.heading: Pitfalls to avoid
bullets: Applying ayat to modern events without knowledge
teach.note: Warn against claiming that a personal idea is the meaning of an ayah. Explain that qualified scholars study Arabic, Qur'an sciences and the Sunnah. A good habit: say 'scholars have said...' and cite. Ask: what is the harm of quoting an ayah without context?

teach.heading: When to ask
bullets: Say 'I do not know' when needed
teach.note: Teach humility: knowing the limits of our knowledge is part of good adab. Pupils write a question they would take to a scholar. Close with a dua for understanding.

practice: Complete 4:43: 'do not approach prayer while intoxicated, until...'
Why is it important to read the full ayah?
Name two tafsirs.
independent: Find the full context of 2:256 in a tafsir and summarise it
Rewrite a mis-quoted half ayah with its full text
Write a code of conduct for quoting the Qur'an
exit: Why can a translation never replace the Arabic?
Name one way to avoid misusing an ayah.
lessons.homework: Choose an ayah you know, read its tafsir and write a short summary with its context.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: scaffolded tafsir reading with a glossary. Stretch: compare two tafsir explanations of one ayah.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Teaching, recital and a lifelong plan
lessons.title: Teaching the Qur'an: planning a mini lesson
objectives: Explain why teaching the Qur'an is valued
Plan a five-minute mini lesson on one tajweed rule
Give and receive feedback on teaching

keywords.def: teaching
to show clearly how something is done
repeat after the teacher, one phrase at a time

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.
Recite 18:1-5.
What is one rule you can explain confidently?

teach.heading: A great reward
bullets: Bukhari: the best of you learn the Qur'an and teach it
teach.note: Quote the hadith reported by Uthman in Sahih al-Bukhari: the best of you are those who learn the Qur'an and teach it. Ask: why is teaching a form of ihsan? Remind pupils to teach for Allah, not to impress.

teach.heading: Plan a mini lesson
bullets: Choose one rule and one example
Let the learner echo, then try alone
teach.note: Show the structure: aim, model, echo, practise, check. Model with a rule such as ikhfa using a short phrase. Pupils choose their own rule and an ayah as the example. Ask: which examples are clearest?

teach.heading: Teaching well
bullets: Correct one thing at a time
teach.note: Link to the lesson on correction. Give feedback phrases. Remind pupils that a teacher also learns: when you teach, you notice your own mistakes. Ask: what would you say to someone who is nervous?

teach.heading: Know your limits
teach.note: Teach humility: pupils may teach basic rules to family and younger pupils but should refer to qualified teachers for difficult questions. Discuss: who taught you the Qur'an? Make dua for them.

teach.heading: Peer practice
bullets: Teach your mini lesson to a partner
Partner gives one strength, one target
teach.note: In breakout pairs, pupils deliver the five-minute lesson. The partner uses the checklist. Return to the main room and share one good idea. Collect plans for display.

practice: What does the hadith in Bukhari say about the best of us?
What are the five steps of a mini lesson?
How should you answer a question you cannot answer?
independent: Write a mini lesson plan for one rule
Teach it to a partner and note feedback
Improve your plan using the feedback
exit: Why should we teach with sincerity?
Name two qualities of a good teacher of the Qur'an.
lessons.homework: Teach your mini lesson to a family member or younger sibling and note what went well.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: mini lesson template with sentence frames. Stretch: plan a series of three short lessons on one theme.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Teaching, recital and a lifelong plan
lessons.title: Recital assessment and a lifelong plan with the Qur'an
objectives: Recite a chosen passage with the rubric
Self-assess and peer-assess
Write a plan for keeping and living by the Qur'an

keywords.def: a set of criteria for judging quality
steadfastness
revision

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.
Recite the isti'adha and basmalah.
Which passage will you recite today?

teach.heading: Prepare
teach.note: Give five minutes to prepare quietly. Remind pupils of adab: sincere intention, calm place, a short dua. Reduce nerves; this is a chance to show growth over the years.

teach.heading: Rubric
teach.note: Share the rubric. Pupils recite individually or in pairs. Mark with the rubric. Give feedback as one strength, one target, one action. Make it warm and encouraging.

teach.heading: Recite and listen
teach.note: Pupils recite in turn. The listener practises adab: silence, attention and kindness. Remind them of 7:204 on listening to the Qur'an. Keep good humour and respect.

teach.heading: Look back
teach.note: Pupils return to their tajweed map from Lesson 1. They tick progress and note remaining gaps. Share a few successes aloud and thank Allah for them.

teach.heading: My lifelong plan
bullets: Daily: a few minutes of recitation
teach.note: Pupils write a realistic plan for the years after school: daily time, a revision cycle (sabaq, sabqi, manzil), a teacher or study circle, and one meaning-based habit. Close with a dua for steadfastness and for Allah to make the Qur'an the spring of our hearts.

practice: Which rule family is strongest for you?
Which family needs more work in the future?
independent: Recite your chosen passage for assessment
Complete peer feedback with the rubric
Write your lifelong plan with dates for review
exit: Name one strength in your recitation.
Name one habit you will keep after school.
lessons.homework: Share your plan with a parent or teacher and ask them to check in with you each month.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: simplified rubric with sentence frames. Stretch: mentor a younger pupil on one rule.
